60 year old female with joint pains"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Welcome to my blog! I am Varshitha Kalidindi, a 4th year medical student. This is an e-log to discuss our patient's de-identified health data after taking informed consent of the patient. It also reflects patient centered online learning portfolio.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI will be looking forward to some feedback and valuable inputs through the comments box provided below.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI have been given this case in an attempt to understand the topic of \"patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations, diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECASE:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 60 year old female, who was an agricultural labourer by occupation (but has stopped working since 4 years), came to the hospital with complaints of\u0026nbsp; pain in both knees since 4-5 years, facial swelling since 2-3 months, pedal edema since 1 week.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic 4-5 years ago. She then started developing pain in both her knees which is aggravated on walking and standing, relieved on resting and medications (painkillers). She stopped working due to the pains.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2-3 months ago, she developed facial puffiness which was insidious in onset and gradually progressive in nature. It appears maximally in the mornings and gets relieved by the end of the day.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1 month ago, she had a tooth extraction on the left side and still has facial puffiness on the left side.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1 week ago, she had pedal edema upto her ankles which was pitting in nature. This also appears maximally in the morning and subsides by the end of the day. Her edema greatly subsided by itself after a week.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe came to the hospital now to find a working solution for her joint pains and to find out about why her pedal edema appeared and disappeared.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDAILY ROUTINE:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient wakes up in the morning at 5:30 and begins household chores, eats breakfast at 8:00. She smokes tobacco at this time.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe then passes her time by talking with family members or guests till 11:00, when she cooks her lunch and eats lunch late, around 3:00-4:00pm\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe has tea occasionally in between, when she visits family. She spends time sleeping or talking with friends and family in person or on the phone.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt night, she doesn't feel hungry. She may or may not smoke tobacco again. She then sleeps at around 10:00pm.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis has been her routine since 4 years, after she stopped working.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPAST HISTORY:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of diabetes, hypertension, CVA, CAD, TB, asthma\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFAMILY HISTORY:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot significant.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETREATMENT HISTORY:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient has a history of using NSAIDS 3-4 days a week since 4 years for the joint pains, suggested by and RMP.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite: normal\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiet: mixed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESleep: adequate\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel movements: regular\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMicturition: normal\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo known allergies\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAddictions: Smokes tobacco once or twice a day everyday\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMENSTRUAL HISTORY:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAttained menopause 20 years ago\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOBSTETRIC HISTORY:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAge at marriage: 18 yrs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAge at first childbirth: 20\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EObstetric formula: G5P5L5\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAll normal vaginal deliveries\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGENERAL EXAMINATION:-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient is conscious, coherent, cooperative and well-oriented to time, place and person.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient is moderately built and well-nourished.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, koilonychia,
